name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (domain=job/equip rule, inventory system). Descriptor accurately reflects purpose: returns 1 if the char's job permits equipping the given item, else 0. No Ghidra address residue in the name.
purpose: Job/equipment compatibility check: returns 1 if char_idx's current job permits equipping item_id, else 0.
logic_summary: allowed_types = fd2_get_job_allowed_items_table_entry(runtime_char[char_idx].job_id) -> pointer to the job's 7-byte table entry (first 6 bytes are allowed item-type ids, 7th is a trailing terminator/flag). item_category = fd2_get_item_effect_entry(item_id)[0]. Scan the first 6 entries of allowed_types (asm: CMP EAX,6 / JGE); return 1 on the first match of item_category, else 0. EBX holds item_category (MOVZX-loaded once, callee-saved), ESI holds the allowed_types pointer; trailing POP ESI/POP EBX/RET is the shared epilogue. __CHK(0x10) stack-probe prologue is compiler-injected.

params.name: char_idx
params.semantics: Runtime-character index into data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr; its job_id selects the job's allowed-item-types table entry.
params.reason: Ghidra live name is the generic placeholder param_1; src already uses char_idx which accurately reflects use (runtime_char index whose job_id drives the lookup). Rename applied in Stage 2.

params.name: item_id
params.semantics: Item id passed to fd2_get_item_effect_entry; its category byte (entry+0) is compared against the job's allowed types.
params.reason: Ghidra live name is the generic placeholder param_2; src already uses item_id which accurately reflects use (item whose category byte is checked). Rename applied in Stage 2.

returns.semantics: 1 = job may equip the item (item category matched one of the first 6 allowed types); 0 = not allowed.

comment_original_issue: None. The src comment block accurately and concisely describes purpose, the 7-byte/scan-first-6 detail (matching asm CMP EAX,6 / JGE), both callers, and the __CHK(0x10) prologue; all verified against decompile and disassembly. Kept as-is.
notes: Verified via decompile + disassembly: loop bound CMP EAX,0x6/JGE (scans first 6 of the 7-byte job table entry); fd2_get_job_allowed_items_table_entry @ 0x4E53E confirmed 7-byte stride per job (6 allowed-type bytes + 1 trailing). Callers fd2_equip_unequip_inventory_menu @ 0x1BFFE and fd2_run_buy_item_menu @ 0x2F0B0 confirmed via get_function_callers + xrefs. Sole global read = data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr @ 0x53A45 (asm reads [0x00053A45]); no writes. Ghidra plate (zh) calls the entry a '6-byte permitted-types array' which is only mildly imprecise about the 7-byte stride, but is not contradictory with what THIS function scans (6 permitted-type bytes) and the authoritative stride detail already lives in the accessor's own plate; left plate unchanged per the keep-unless-contradictory rule. Only this shard staged for commit (src/ui_menu/status.c unmodified).
